siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn on this record's stable key from the stocks its household class may hang (5 in, 5.5 in or 6 in; T-1839, docs/LIBERTIES.md L352), then advanced within them so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

land_owner.value: The ground was entered by Robert A Kenzie, 7 May 1831
land_owner.note: KINZIE'S ADDITION. The north fraction of section 10 is the section north of the river, which is why the register prints 102.29 acres and not a quarter's 160. It is resolved as the section's own grid box clipped to the committed north bank of the main stem (`e1834_harbor_cut/shoreline.geojson`), so no boundary here is authored. The two rows the register carries for it — one plain, one with the school-section marker — are the same entry printed twice. THE REGISTER SPELLS THE PURCHASER MORE THAN ONE WAY for this same tract — Robert A Kenzie; Robert A Kinzie — and the spellings are carried rather than merged, which is the land_sales crosswalk's standing rule: tract agreement is where two spellings MIGHT be one man and is never proof that they are. THE ROOF IS AN INVENTION AND THIS CANNOT OUTRANK IT. The footprint stands 83 m inside the tract's nearest boundary, which on a documented building would carry the middle tier, but this building was dealt to its lot by a recipe and is not there. The tract is real and the register's words about it are read; what is graded here is the claim that THIS roof stands on it, and that claim is the recipe's. WHAT THIS ROW CLAIMS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It claims that the tract the Illinois State Archives' land-sale register describes contains this structure's committed position — the patent for this ground was ENTERED by this man on this date. It does not claim he still held the ground on 1 July 1835, that he lived here, or that he ever stood on it: a sale is a transaction, and the register's only column about residence names a county. THE SECTION LINES ARE CONSTRUCTED, NOT TRACED (L219): the grid is carried from the single PLSS corner at State & Madison, on the plat's own east-west bearing, in nominal one-mile squares.

persons.name: H. Y. Crane
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Crane, H. Y.' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.

persons.name: Leonard C. Hugunin
persons.note: INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED RESIDENT. Originally documented in Chicago post-office evidence; independent resident research now corroborates the identity. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print '• Hugunin, Leonard, C.' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 5 — dated 1835-07-01. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1). FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “L. C. Hugunin” (f1839_v0430, printed page 44, ward 3, voting for William B. Ogden). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Hugunin' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins L. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

persons.name: D O Robinson
persons.note: A CONTEMPORARY CHICAGO PAPER OF 1833-1835 PRINTS THIS PERSON BY NAME IN THE TOWN. Read from newspaper_1833_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1b), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 20 May 1835 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1).
